notes: FOUR ANSWERS ON THE BANK RECONCILIATION SCREEN. AN ADJUSTMENT YOU HAVE BOOKED CAN NOW BE TAKEN BACK. Other adjustments posts a real voucher — a bank charge debits an expense and credits the bank, interest does the reverse — and until now the row simply disappeared afterwards. Nothing kept the voucher it became, and undoing one meant finding the journal in the Approval Centre, where it reversed as an ordinary ledger entry with nothing to tell the reconciliation it had gone. Booked adjustments are now listed under BOOKED TO THE LEDGER ON THIS DATE, each with the voucher it became and each with TAKE BACK. Taking one back reverses it through the ledger own reversal, on its original entry date, and asks why — the reason goes on the reversing voucher. Your difference moves by the amount, which is right: the month had been balanced over an entry that should not have been there. The row stays on the list, marked Taken back, because a month history includes what was undone. MONEY THAT LEAVES THE BANK WITHOUT A CHEQUE IS NOW A RECONCILING ITEM. The reconciliation read the cheque register and the lodgement register and nothing else. But not every payment carries a cheque: a standing order, a direct debit, an ACH transfer, the paying leg of a bank transfer, a statutory remittance keyed as a journal. Each one reduces your cashbook the day it is entered and reaches the statement whenever the bank gets to it, and in between it is a reconciling item exactly as an unpresented cheque is. The month could not tie and nothing on the screen said why. Two new schedules now carry them: LEFT THE BANK WITH NO CHEQUE and REACHED THE BANK WITH NO LODGEMENT. They are subtracted and added on the same reasoning as cheques and lodgements and counted into the same totals. When the statement shows one, press SHOWN and give the bank date; it leaves that month and every month after it, and stays on the months it genuinely belonged to. These are counted from the first statement you imported for the account, never earlier — an account with no statement imported behaves exactly as it does today. A MONTH CAN NO LONGER BE SIGNED OFF OVER A STATEMENT LINE NOBODY HAS ANSWERED FOR. A zero difference was the only gate, and it can hide an unfinished month: mark a cheque presented by hand in the register and both sides move together, so the arithmetic ties while a line on the statement still answers to nothing. Sign-off is now refused until every statement line up to the statement date is matched, posted or set aside, and the button says which gate is closed rather than being quietly disabled. THE YEAR AT A GLANCE. Above History there is now a row of twelve months for the account on screen, each saying what was filed: signed off, draft, or nothing at all. Click one to put that month on the screen above — a month already filed opens with its own figures, an empty one at the month end ready to start. A list of the reconciliations you have done can never show you the month that was skipped; this can. INSTALLING: two new tables and one extended function; no existing data changes, and nothing is counted twice — anything that already carries a cheque, a lodgement, a statement posting or a reconciliation adjustment is left exactly where it is. This installs straight over the previous version. Please still take a backup first: Backup & Export, Back up now.
